title: A connection that cannot be misused
description:
Model a network connection whose rules are checked by the compiler. `Connection<S>` holds a `Vec<String>` log of what happened and a state:

- `Connection::new(host: &str) -> Connection<Closed>` logs `"created <host>"`.
- `Connection<Closed>::open(self) -> Connection<Open>` logs `"opened"`.
- `Connection<Open>::login(self, user: &str, password: &str) -> Result<Connection<Authenticated>, Connection<Open>>`: succeeds (logging `"logged in as <user>"`) when the password is `"secret"`, otherwise logs `"login failed"` and gives the open connection back in `Err` so the caller can try again.
- `Connection<Authenticated>::send(&mut self, message: &str)` logs `"sent <message>"`.
- Both `Connection<Open>` and `Connection<Authenticated>` have `close(self) -> Connection<Closed>` logging `"closed"`; write it once in an `impl<S: CanClose> Connection<S>` with a marker trait `CanClose` implemented for the two states.
- Every state has `log(&self) -> &[String]`.
hints: A small generic helper on `impl<S> Connection<S>`, such as `fn into_state<T>(mut self, entry: String) -> Connection<T>`, adds the log line and rebuilds the struct in the new state: every transition then becomes one line.
`impl<S: CanClose> Connection<S> { fn close(self) ... }` gives `close` to exactly the states that implement the marker trait, and to no others: `Connection<Closed>` has no `close`.
